### 13.9 Honest caveats

a. **Synthetic PointerEvents for canvas work.** The 2827 cell taps and 74 drags are
   `new PointerEvent(..., pointerType:'touch')` dispatched on `#wholeSheetCanvas`, not
   driver-level hardware touch. Two reasons, both structural: the WebKit automation protocol
   exposes only `Input.dispatchTapEvent` (already recorded in §11), and at 126 × 72 cells × 12 px
   the sheet is 1512 × 864 CSS px inside a 750 × 342 viewport, so hardware-coordinate taps would
   require a pan or zoom operation per cell. All twelve *control* taps in the recipe were real
   `page.tap()`.
b. **No physical hardware.** No real device, no real finger, no OS share sheet was dismissed by a
   human. The share call was accepted by the WebKit context; nothing verifies what an iOS share
   sheet would then do with the file.
c. **`wm-04-after-L0.png` comes from a second, separate 29-step run**
   (`execute_l0_shot.mjs`), not from the main run. In the main run the step-29 screenshot hook sat
   behind the batched `tap_cell` branch and never fired — a driver bug, not a UI finding. The
   supplementary run re-executed recipe steps 1–29 in the same mobile context and verified
   `{"layers":3,"cols":126,"rows":72,"L0_mismatches":0}` before capturing. Layer 0 correctness *in
   the main run* is established by the step-114 checkpoint, which re-verifies all three layers.
d. **Colour inputs were value-seeded.** `#wsFgColor` / `#wsBgColor` are `input[type=color]`; their
   pickers are OS-native and undrivable. The 51 colour changes set `.value` and dispatched
   `input` + `change`, which is what the handlers listen on. Every other field was really typed.
e. **`select_layer` used `element.click()`** on the real `.ws-layer-row`, not `page.tap()` — the row
   is a real control with its own click handler, but the tap was not driver-level.
f. **The recipe, not free-hand authoring.** This run proves the recipe reproduces the target through
   the mobile UI. It does not claim a human would discover this 3031-action sequence unaided; the
   obstacle table in `audit.md` §5 documents what made it this long (chiefly the defective `Flip V`,
   which forces both projection halves to be painted cell by cell).
g. **Layer 2 art was painted with the transparent fill already down**, so the 2820 art taps overwrite
   fill cells rather than empty ones — matching the simulation, and confirmed by every checkpoint.
